thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2-gpu-pool. Autoscaler hitting max replicas. Error rate increasing. Trigger: queue_length > 95th percentile for 6m. thread_ts=2612345678
alyssa: seeing it — dashboard shows sustained queue ~1200 reqs, autoscaler capped at 120 nodes. latency p50 -> 420ms, p95 -> 1.8s. :frowning_face:
dustin: paging infra oncall. suspecting driver instability causing nodes to drop out of pool, effective capacity lower than reported. will run quick health sweep.
morris: copying logs from one of the flapping nodes:```
[2026-03-15T02:34:01Z] nvidia: Xid (PCIe) 31, GPU hung
[2026-03-15T02:34:02Z] kernel: oom_killer: kill process 2345 (driverd) total-vm:123456kB
[2026-03-15T02:34:05Z] containerd: container exited 137
```
leo: confirmed multiple nodes showing Xid 31 and repeated OOMs. kubelet marks pods NotReady then they rejoin but KV cache lost, long warmup.
alyssa: customer impact estimate (prelim): hosted text-gen endpoints experiencing 5xx spikes. Top affected tenants: DataMuse (error surge), ShopFlux (latency), HealthSight (degraded throughput). hitting support SLAs for 3 customers.
cust-sre: flagged DataMuse incident; they've reported timeouts since ~02:30 UTC. ticket ID DM-8134.
ops-rotation: I'm taking lead. immediate mitigations: 1) cordon the most unstable nodes to stop scheduling new request-shards, 2) reduce concurrency on replicas to lower driver memory pressure, 3) temporarily raise autoscaler soft limit to allow additional nodes where possible. executing now.
dustin: running quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=us-west-2-gpu -o wide | grep NotReady` -> 7 NotReady, 65 Ready. but Ready count is deceiving, several showing >90% GPU memory fragmentation.
morris: rolling driver restart plan: will restart nvidia-host-agent on affected nodes in small batches (3 at a time). command:```bash
ssh node-${N}; sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver-host; journalctl -u nvidia-driver-host -n 200
```
alyssa: can we also throttle intake? Add a temporary per-customer rate-limit for heavy gen routes to reduce queue backlog. Dustin can you flip the gate?
dustin: applying temporary route cap now. PATCH to gateway config:```json
{"/v1/generate":{"rate_limit_per_min":6000}}
```
ops-rotation: autoscaler bump: current max_replicas=120. I'm setting max_replicas=180 for us-west-2 for 30 minutes to buy us time. executing: `curl -XPOST https://infra-api/scale?pool=us-west-2-gpu&max=180`
leo: note — we might hit infra quota in us-west-2; failover fallback to us-east-1 will require model routing compatibility. can we enable multi-region spill?
alyssa: enabling cross-region fallback for non-data-residency-sensitive tenants. will update routing policy.
morris: after first restart batch (nodes 12-14) I see Xid stops for those nodes, GPUs back to normal. but one node returned repeated Xid after 20m. collecting dmesg: `E NVRM: Xid 79, GPU exception` - looks like kernel/driver mismatch on that host.
dustin: I'm in contact with cloud provider support; opened case CP-4321. they've acknowledged possible host-level firmware flakiness.
cust-sre: DataMuse notified of mitigation steps and temporary rate limits. they acknowledged.
ops-rotation: quick status 02:50 UTC — queue length down from 1200 -> 420, error rate decreasing ~64%, latency starting to normalize. still watching for recurrence.
alyssa: retained evidence: please attach these node-level logs to the incident ticket. we'll need a postmortem with root cause and remediation (driver pinning, firmware audit, autoscaler dynamic headroom).
dustin: temporary config changes: autoscaler max bumped, gateway rate-limits applied, cross-region spill enabled for eligible tenants. Documenting commands in ops-runbook.
leo: follow-up item — add health probe that checks driver Xid counts and GPU memory fragmentation before node is considered Ready. will propose change.
morris: +1 on health probe. also propose rolling driver kernel compatibility check on boot.
ops-rotation: handing off to next oncall (michael) for 03:00-07:00 shift. summary pinned: GPUs in us-west-2 experienced driver OOM/Xid cascade reducing usable capacity; mitigations: node cordon, driver restarts in batches, autoscaler max increased, temporary rate-limits, cross-region spill. customer impact: transient 5xxs and elevated latency for a subset of tenants; DataMuse ticket DM-8134 created.
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: ACTIONS logged: escalate to infra-eng for driver/firmware investigation; schedule postmortem; update runbook with probe. incident priority: P1 -> monitoring window 72h.
alyssa: thanks team. please add any followups to the incident thread. I'll draft a short status update for support + affected customers. :thumbsup:
ops-rotation: :thumbsup: I'm leaving the temporary autoscaler bump active for 30m more, then we'll reassess.
michael: taking over. reading thread now.
